title: The Library Slip Found inside the Wrong Book
sentences: On Monday, Emi borrowed a science book from the school library.
At home, a yellow slip fell from the book.
The slip had Koji's name and Friday's date, but the title on it was a history book.
Emi first thought the library had put the wrong slip in her science book.
Then she noticed a small call number on the slip and compared it with the number on her book.
The numbers were different, so she took the slip to the library without writing on it.
The librarian checked the return cart and found Koji's history book there.
Its pocket was empty, so the librarian returned the yellow slip to that book.
Emi learned to use several clues to identify where a paper belongs.

slashRows.en: On Monday, Emi borrowed a science book from the school library.
slashRows.jp: 月曜日、恵美は学校の図書館で理科の本を借りました。

slashRows.en: At home, a yellow slip fell from the book.
slashRows.jp: 家で開くと、本から黄色い貸出票が落ちました。

slashRows.en: The slip had Koji's name and Friday's date, but the title on it was a history book.
slashRows.jp: 貸出票には浩二の名前と金曜日の日付がありましたが、書かれていた題名は歴史の本でした。

slashRows.en: Emi first thought the library had put the wrong slip in her science book.
slashRows.jp: 恵美は最初、図書館が理科の本に間違った貸出票を入れたのだと思いました。

slashRows.en: Then she noticed a small call number on the slip and compared it with the number on her book.
slashRows.jp: そこで貸出票の小さな請求番号に気づき、自分の本の番号と比べました。

slashRows.en: The numbers were different, so she took the slip to the library without writing on it.
slashRows.jp: 番号は違っていたので、何も書き込まず貸出票を図書館へ持って行きました。

slashRows.en: The librarian checked the return cart and found Koji's history book there.
slashRows.jp: 司書が返却用の台車を調べると、そこに浩二の歴史の本がありました。

slashRows.en: Its pocket was empty, so the librarian returned the yellow slip to that book.
slashRows.jp: その本のポケットは空だったため、司書は黄色い貸出票をその本へ戻しました。

slashRows.en: Emi learned to use several clues to identify where a paper belongs.
slashRows.jp: 恵美は、複数の手がかりで紙の正しい場所を確かめられると学びました。

title: The Seed Cups Watered by Two Groups
sentences: Class 1-A planted bean seeds in twelve paper cups by the classroom window.
The morning group watered them and marked Monday on the care sheet.
After lunch, the afternoon group saw dry soil on top and watered every cup again.
The next day, two cups had water standing at the bottom, and one seed had moved above the soil.
The sheet showed that both groups had watered the cups on Monday.
They kept caring for the plants, but they changed the job record.
From Tuesday, each student wrote a name and time after the job.
The second group checked the record and watered only when no earlier mark was there.
The class learned that shared work needs a clear record.

slashRows.en: Class 1-A planted bean seeds in twelve paper cups by the classroom window.
slashRows.jp: 一年A組は教室の窓辺で十二個の紙コップに豆の種を植えました。

slashRows.en: The morning group watered them and marked Monday on the care sheet.
slashRows.jp: 朝の班は水をやり、世話の表の月曜日に印を付けました。

slashRows.en: After lunch, the afternoon group saw dry soil on top and watered every cup again.
slashRows.jp: 昼食後、午後の班は表面の土が乾いているのを見て、全部のコップにもう一度水をやりました。

slashRows.en: The next day, two cups had water standing at the bottom, and one seed had moved above the soil.
slashRows.jp: 翌日、二つのコップの底に水がたまり、一つの種は土の上へ動いていました。

slashRows.en: The sheet showed that both groups had watered the cups on Monday.
slashRows.jp: 表を見ると、月曜日に二つの班が水をやっていたと分かりました。

slashRows.en: They kept caring for the plants, but they changed the job record.
slashRows.jp: 植物の世話は続けましたが、作業の記録方法を変えました。

slashRows.en: From Tuesday, each student wrote a name and time after the job.
slashRows.jp: 火曜日からは、各生徒が作業後に名前と時刻を書くことにしました。

slashRows.en: The second group checked the record and watered only when no earlier mark was there.
slashRows.jp: 二つ目の班は記録を確かめ、前の印がないときだけ水をやりました。

slashRows.en: The class learned that shared work needs a clear record.
slashRows.jp: クラスは、共同作業には明確な記録が必要だと学びました。

title: A Morning Meeting Moved for Floor Cleaning
sentences: The student council planned a short meeting in Room 2 before school on Wednesday.
On Tuesday afternoon, a notice said cleaners would clean the second-floor rooms early Wednesday.
A new council message moved the meeting to the library at the same time.
Kenta had written Room 2 in his notebook on Monday and almost followed that older plan.
Before leaving home, he checked the message time and saw that the library notice was newer.
He went directly to the library instead of checking Room 2 first.
All members arrived there before the meeting began, while cleaners worked upstairs.
Afterward, the council added the word 'CHANGED' to future room-change messages.
Kenta learned to follow the newest dated notice after a schedule change.

slashRows.en: The student council planned a short meeting in Room 2 before school on Wednesday.
slashRows.jp: 生徒会は水曜日の登校前に二番教室で短い会議をする予定でした。

slashRows.en: On Tuesday afternoon, a notice said cleaners would clean the second-floor rooms early Wednesday.
slashRows.jp: 火曜日の午後、水曜日の朝早く清掃員が二階の教室を清掃するという案内が出ました。

slashRows.en: A new council message moved the meeting to the library at the same time.
slashRows.jp: 新しい生徒会連絡は、同じ時刻のまま会議を図書館へ変更しました。

slashRows.en: Kenta had written Room 2 in his notebook on Monday and almost followed that older plan.
slashRows.jp: 健太は月曜日にノートへ二番教室と書いており、その古い予定に従いそうになりました。

slashRows.en: Before leaving home, he checked the message time and saw that the library notice was newer.
slashRows.jp: 家を出る前に連絡の時刻を確認すると、図書館への変更の方が新しいと分かりました。

slashRows.en: He went directly to the library instead of checking Room 2 first.
slashRows.jp: 健太は二番教室を先に見に行かず、直接図書館へ向かいました。

slashRows.en: All members arrived there before the meeting began, while cleaners worked upstairs.
slashRows.jp: 全員が会議開始前に図書館へ集まり、その間二階では清掃が行われました。

slashRows.en: Afterward, the council added the word 'CHANGED' to future room-change messages.
slashRows.jp: その後、生徒会は今後の場所変更の連絡に「変更」と目立つよう書くことにしました。

slashRows.en: Kenta learned to follow the newest dated notice after a schedule change.
slashRows.jp: 健太は、予定変更後は最新の日付の連絡に従うと学びました。

title: The Bottle with a Music Club Sticker
sentences: After school, Rina found a blue water bottle under a bench near the gym.
Three classmates had similar bottles, so color did not show the owner.
A small music-note sticker was on the bottom, and the name area was unclear.
Rina remembered that the music club had practiced in the gym that afternoon.
She did not give the bottle to a classmate who simply said it looked like his.
She took it to the music room and asked whether anyone used the same sticker.
Mao showed the matching sticker on her music folder and described a scratch beside the cap.
The scratch matched, so Rina returned the bottle to Mao.
Rina learned that matching details are stronger clues than appearance alone.

slashRows.en: After school, Rina found a blue water bottle under a bench near the gym.
slashRows.jp: 放課後、里奈は体育館近くのベンチの下で青い水筒を見つけました。

slashRows.en: Three classmates had similar bottles, so color did not show the owner.
slashRows.jp: クラスに似た水筒を持つ生徒が三人いたため、色だけでは持ち主が分かりませんでした。

slashRows.en: A small music-note sticker was on the bottom, and the name area was unclear.
slashRows.jp: 底には小さな音符のシールがあり、名前を書く部分は不鮮明でした。

slashRows.en: Rina remembered that the music club had practiced in the gym that afternoon.
slashRows.jp: 里奈はその日の午後、音楽部が体育館で練習していたことを思い出しました。

slashRows.en: She did not give the bottle to a classmate who simply said it looked like his.
slashRows.jp: 見た目が似ていると言っただけのクラスメートには渡しませんでした。

slashRows.en: She took it to the music room and asked whether anyone used the same sticker.
slashRows.jp: 音楽室へ持って行き、同じシールを使っている人がいるか尋ねました。

slashRows.en: Mao showed the matching sticker on her music folder and described a scratch beside the cap.
slashRows.jp: 真央は音楽ファイルの同じシールを見せ、ふたの横の傷についても説明しました。

slashRows.en: The scratch matched, so Rina returned the bottle to Mao.
slashRows.jp: 傷も一致したため、里奈は水筒を真央へ返しました。

slashRows.en: Rina learned that matching details are stronger clues than appearance alone.
slashRows.jp: 里奈は、一致する細部は見た目だけより強い手がかりだと学びました。

title: A Lunch Tray Count after the Class Trip Changed
sentences: The lunch staff prepared trays for thirty-two students in Class 1-C.
That morning, eight students left school for a half-day class trip before lunch.
The old lunch list still showed thirty-two students.
Yuna counted the class and found twenty-four students in the classroom.
She did not throw away the extra lunches or guess who needed them.
She told the teacher before lunch service and showed the new class count.
The teacher called the lunch room, which had not yet placed food on the extra trays.
The lunch room sent only twenty-four trays, and the extra trays stayed clean for another class.
Yuna learned to update quantities when the number of people changes.

slashRows.en: The lunch staff prepared trays for thirty-two students in Class 1-C.
slashRows.jp: 給食係は一年C組の三十二人分のトレーを準備しました。

slashRows.en: That morning, eight students left school for a half-day class trip before lunch.
slashRows.jp: その朝、八人の生徒が昼食前から半日の校外学習へ出かけました。

slashRows.en: The old lunch list still showed thirty-two students.
slashRows.jp: 古い給食表はまだ三十二人のままでした。

slashRows.en: Yuna counted the class and found twenty-four students in the classroom.
slashRows.jp: 優奈がクラスの人数を数えると、教室には二十四人いました。

slashRows.en: She did not throw away the extra lunches or guess who needed them.
slashRows.jp: 余った給食を捨てたり、誰が必要かを推測したりしませんでした。

slashRows.en: She told the teacher before lunch service and showed the new class count.
slashRows.jp: 給食を配る前に先生へ伝え、新しい人数を示しました。

slashRows.en: The teacher called the lunch room, which had not yet placed food on the extra trays.
slashRows.jp: 先生が給食室へ連絡すると、余分なトレーにはまだ食べ物が載せられていませんでした。

slashRows.en: The lunch room sent only twenty-four trays, and the extra trays stayed clean for another class.
slashRows.jp: 給食室は二十四人分だけを送り、余分なトレーはきれいなまま別のクラスに使えました。

slashRows.en: Yuna learned to update quantities when the number of people changes.
slashRows.jp: 優奈は、人数が変われば必要数も更新すると学びました。

title: The Notebook Pages Mixed by an Open Window
sentences: Haruto left his project notebook open while carrying books.
A strong wind came through the window and blew four loose pages onto the floor.
The pages had no numbers, but each ended by leading to the next step.
One page described planting seeds, another showed the first leaves, and a third recorded flowers.
Haruto did not put them back in the order in which he picked them up.
He read the dates and the changes in the plant from each page.
The seed page came first, the leaf page followed it, and the flower record came later.
He clipped the pages together and added page numbers before closing the window.
Haruto learned to restore lost page order from dates and events.

slashRows.en: Haruto left his project notebook open while carrying books.
slashRows.jp: 陽斗は本を運ぶ間、調べ学習ノートを開いたままにしました。

slashRows.en: A strong wind came through the window and blew four loose pages onto the floor.
slashRows.jp: 強い風が窓から入り、四枚のページが床へ飛びました。

slashRows.en: The pages had no numbers, but each ended by leading to the next step.
slashRows.jp: ページ番号はありませんでしたが、各ページ末は次の段階につながっていました。

slashRows.en: One page described planting seeds, another showed the first leaves, and a third recorded flowers.
slashRows.jp: 一枚は種まき、別の一枚は最初の葉、三枚目は花について書かれていました。

slashRows.en: Haruto did not put them back in the order in which he picked them up.
slashRows.jp: 陽斗は拾った順番のまま戻しませんでした。

slashRows.en: He read the dates and the changes in the plant from each page.
slashRows.jp: 各ページの日付と植物の変化を読みました。

slashRows.en: The seed page came first, the leaf page followed it, and the flower record came later.
slashRows.jp: 種のページが最初で、その後に葉、さらに後に花の記録が続きました。

slashRows.en: He clipped the pages together and added page numbers before closing the window.
slashRows.jp: ページを留め、ページ番号を付けてから窓を閉めました。

slashRows.en: Haruto learned to restore lost page order from dates and events.
slashRows.jp: 陽斗は、日付と出来事から失われたページ順を戻せると学びました。

title: A Relay Order Changed after a Student Hurt a Foot
sentences: Four students practiced a relay for the school sports day.
Their usual order was Aki, Ren, Yuto, and Mei, and Yuto ran the long third section.
During Tuesday practice, Yuto hurt his foot, and the nurse said, “Do not run tomorrow.”
The team first thought about leaving his place empty, but a relay needed four runners.
They asked reserve runner Saki which section she had practiced.
Saki had practiced the second section, so Ren moved to Yuto's longer third section.
The new order became Aki, Saki, Ren, and Mei, and they practiced the two changed handoffs.
Yuto watched from the side and helped check their marks instead of running.
The team learned that a safe replacement also changes the surrounding order.

slashRows.en: Four students practiced a relay for the school sports day.
slashRows.jp: 四人の生徒が運動会のリレー練習をしていました。

slashRows.en: Their usual order was Aki, Ren, Yuto, and Mei, and Yuto ran the long third section.
slashRows.jp: いつもの順番は秋、蓮、悠斗、芽衣で、悠斗が長い第三区間を走っていました。

slashRows.en: During Tuesday practice, Yuto hurt his foot, and the nurse said, “Do not run tomorrow.”
slashRows.jp: 火曜日の練習中に悠斗が足を痛め、保健の先生は「明日は走らないで」と言いました。

slashRows.en: The team first thought about leaving his place empty, but a relay needed four runners.
slashRows.jp: チームは最初その場所を空けようと考えましたが、リレーには四人の走者が必要でした。

slashRows.en: They asked reserve runner Saki which section she had practiced.
slashRows.jp: 控えの咲に、どの区間を練習していたか確認しました。

slashRows.en: Saki had practiced the second section, so Ren moved to Yuto's longer third section.
slashRows.jp: 咲は第二区間を練習していたため、蓮が悠斗の長い第三区間へ移りました。

slashRows.en: The new order became Aki, Saki, Ren, and Mei, and they practiced the two changed handoffs.
slashRows.jp: 新しい順番は秋、咲、蓮、芽衣となり、変わった二つのバトン渡しを練習しました。

slashRows.en: Yuto watched from the side and helped check their marks instead of running.
slashRows.jp: 悠斗は走らず横から見て、目印の確認を手伝いました。

slashRows.en: The team learned that a safe replacement also changes the surrounding order.
slashRows.jp: チームは、安全な交代では周りの順序も変わると学びました。

title: The Flower Vase Moved away from the Heater
sentences: The class placed a vase of white flowers on a shelf for an open-school day.
By the next morning, the flowers nearest the classroom heater were bending down.
The water level was still high, so Nami looked at the space around the vase.
She felt warm dry air blowing from the heater onto the flowers.
Nami did not add more water because the vase was already nearly full.
With the teacher, she moved the vase to a bright table away from the hot air.
They marked both positions and compared the flowers again that afternoon.
The moved flowers were no longer bending as quickly, although the damaged ones did not become new again.
Nami learned to change a condition that matched the observed problem.

slashRows.en: The class placed a vase of white flowers on a shelf for an open-school day.
slashRows.jp: クラスは学校公開日のため白い花の花瓶を棚に置きました。

slashRows.en: By the next morning, the flowers nearest the classroom heater were bending down.
slashRows.jp: 翌朝、教室の暖房に最も近い花が下を向いていました。

slashRows.en: The water level was still high, so Nami looked at the space around the vase.
slashRows.jp: 水はまだ十分あったため、奈美は花瓶の周りを確認しました。

slashRows.en: She felt warm dry air blowing from the heater onto the flowers.
slashRows.jp: 暖房から暖かく乾いた風が花へ当たっていると分かりました。

slashRows.en: Nami did not add more water because the vase was already nearly full.
slashRows.jp: 花瓶には十分な水があったので、さらに水を足しませんでした。

slashRows.en: With the teacher, she moved the vase to a bright table away from the hot air.
slashRows.jp: 先生と一緒に、熱い風から離れた明るい机へ花瓶を移しました。

slashRows.en: They marked both positions and compared the flowers again that afternoon.
slashRows.jp: 二つの場所を記録し、その日の午後に花をもう一度比べました。

slashRows.en: The moved flowers were no longer bending as quickly, although the damaged ones did not become new again.
slashRows.jp: 移した花は急にはしおれなくなりましたが、傷んだ花が元通りになるわけではありませんでした。

slashRows.en: Nami learned to change a condition that matched the observed problem.
slashRows.jp: 奈美は、観察した問題に合う条件を変えると学びました。

title: The Old Entrance Still Shown on a School Map
sentences: A printed school map showed visitors entering through the east gate.
On Friday, Kota saw a new sign outside: “Visitors, use the south gate.”
Construction had closed the east gate, but several old maps were still beside the station.
Kota checked the date at the bottom of one map and saw a date from last year.
He kept the map because many roads were still correct.
He told the teacher, and they placed a bright correction sticker over the old entrance arrow.
The sticker directed visitors to the south gate until construction ended.
The school also put a new digital map online and marked the old printed copies clearly.
Kota learned that an old map sometimes needs one important current correction.

slashRows.en: A printed school map showed visitors entering through the east gate.
slashRows.jp: 印刷された学校地図では、来訪者は東門から入るようになっていました。

slashRows.en: On Friday, Kota saw a new sign outside: “Visitors, use the south gate.”
slashRows.jp: 金曜日、航太は外の新しい案内に「来訪者は南門を使ってください」と書かれているのを見ました。

slashRows.en: Construction had closed the east gate, but several old maps were still beside the station.
slashRows.jp: 工事で東門は閉鎖されていましたが、駅のそばには古い地図がまだ何枚か置かれていました。

slashRows.en: Kota checked the date at the bottom of one map and saw a date from last year.
slashRows.jp: 航太が地図の下の日付を見ると、前年の日付だと分かりました。

slashRows.en: He kept the map because many roads were still correct.
slashRows.jp: 多くの道路はまだ正しかったため、その地図を残しました。

slashRows.en: He told the teacher, and they placed a bright correction sticker over the old entrance arrow.
slashRows.jp: 先生に伝え、古い入口の矢印の上に目立つ訂正シールを貼りました。

slashRows.en: The sticker directed visitors to the south gate until construction ended.
slashRows.jp: シールは工事終了まで来訪者を南門へ案内しました。

slashRows.en: The school also put a new digital map online and marked the old printed copies clearly.
slashRows.jp: 学校は新しいデジタル地図も公開し、古い印刷版にははっきり印を付けました。

slashRows.en: Kota learned that an old map sometimes needs one important current correction.
slashRows.jp: 航太は、古い地図には大切な最新の訂正が一つ必要なこともあると学びました。

title: An Eraser Returned inside the Wrong Pencil Case
sentences: Mika found a white eraser inside her pencil case after art class.
She already had her blue eraser, so the white one was not hers.
The white eraser had a small star cut into one corner and a faint letter K.
During art, four pencil cases were together on one table.
Mika did not decide from K alone because two students had K names.
She asked both students to describe the missing erasers before showing it.
Kei said his had a star cut made by his older sister, while Kumi said hers had a red cover.
Mika returned the eraser to Kei and checked her case for other mixed items.
She learned that asking for a detail first can confirm an owner fairly.

slashRows.en: Mika found a white eraser inside her pencil case after art class.
slashRows.jp: 美香は美術の授業後、自分の筆箱の中に白い消しゴムを見つけました。

slashRows.en: She already had her blue eraser, so the white one was not hers.
slashRows.jp: 自分の青い消しゴムがあったため、白い方は自分の物ではありませんでした。

slashRows.en: The white eraser had a small star cut into one corner and a faint letter K.
slashRows.jp: 白い消しゴムの角には小さな星形の切り込みと薄いKの文字がありました。

slashRows.en: During art, four pencil cases were together on one table.
slashRows.jp: 美術の時間、四人分の筆箱が一つの机に置かれていました。

slashRows.en: Mika did not decide from K alone because two students had K names.
slashRows.jp: Kの名前の生徒が二人いたため、文字だけでは決めませんでした。

slashRows.en: She asked both students to describe the missing erasers before showing it.
slashRows.jp: 消しゴムを見せる前に、二人へなくした物の特徴を尋ねました。

slashRows.en: Kei said his had a star cut made by his older sister, while Kumi said hers had a red cover.
slashRows.jp: 圭は姉が星形の切り込みを入れた物だと言い、久美は赤いカバー付きだと言いました。

slashRows.en: Mika returned the eraser to Kei and checked her case for other mixed items.
slashRows.jp: 美香は消しゴムを圭へ返し、ほかの物も自分の筆箱に混ざっていないか確認しました。

slashRows.en: She learned that asking for a detail first can confirm an owner fairly.
slashRows.jp: 美香は、先に特徴を尋ねると公平に持ち主を確認できると学びました。
